concepts.title: Many Kingdoms after the Guptas
concepts.definition: From the sixth to the tenth centuries no single power ruled the subcontinent: kingdoms rose and fell across the north, and the south saw the Pallavas, Pandyas, Chalukyas and, later, the Cholas.
concepts.key_idea: Political division did not stop the flow of trade, temples and texts across the regions.

concepts.title: Kingdoms of the South and the North
concepts.definition: In the Deccan and the south, the Chalukyas and Rashtrakutas, Pallavas and Pandyas built temple cities and fleets, while in the north kingdoms such as those of Harsha and later the Gurjara-Pratiharas held sway.
concepts.key_idea: Region by region, local powers matured: each left its own style of temples, inscriptions and administration.

concepts.title: The Tripartite Struggle
concepts.definition: For over two centuries the Palas, the Gurjara-Pratiharas and the Rashtrakutas fought a tripartite struggle for Kanauj, the prized city on the Ganga; the long war drained all three without a lasting victor.
concepts.formula: struggle = palas + pratiharas + rashtrakutas over kanauj
concepts.key_idea: Kanauj's prestige outvalued its fields: the contest shows how symbol and status drove medieval war.

concepts.title: Learning, Mathematics and Culture
concepts.definition: The age kept learning alive: mathematics and astronomy advanced, Sanskrit kavyas were composed, and temple architecture, from Nagara towers to Dravida vimanas, rose across the land.
concepts.key_idea: Culture outlives dynasties: the maths, poems and temples of this age outlasted every throne that ordered them.
